data.name: Goliath
data.gender_notes: Goliath is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Goliath means ‘hill giant’ or ‘roaring one’. In the Bible, Goliath is a giant Philistine warrior who was famously defeated by David. The name Goliath carries the meaning “Giant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Goliath usually hope their child will grow to embody giant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes overcoming great adversity and trusting in God's strength.
data.etymology: Goliath belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Goliath total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: גוליית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם גוליית מקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו 'גדול וגבהון' או 'המלך הפלישתי הגדול'. גוליית היה ענק פלישתי שנלחם בשל ישראל במערכת עמק האלה, כמתואר בספר שמואל א' בברית החדשה.

in_greek.name: Γολιάθ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Μέγας και Προκλητικός των Φιλιππησίων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Γολιάθ προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ο Μέγας και Προκλητικός' ή 'Ο μεγάλος των Φιλιππησίων'. Ο Γολιάθ ήταν ένας γίγας Φίλιστιος που πολέμησε εναντίον των Ισραηλιτών στην κοιλάδα του Ελαχ, όπως περιγράφεται στο Βιβλίο του Σαμουήλ.

in_latin.name: Goliath
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Goliath originem habet in lingua hebraea et significat 'magnus et excelsus' vel 'rex magnus Philistaeorum'. Goliath fuit gigas Philistaeus qui contra Israelitas pugnavit in valle Elah, ut descriptum est in libro Samuelis.

in_english.name: Goliath
in_english.meaning: a giant Philistine warrior defeated by David
in_english.long_meaning: The name Goliath originates from Hebrew and means 'a giant' or 'a large Philistine warrior'. In biblical context, Goliath was a giant Philistine warrior who fought against the Israelites in the Valley of Elah, as described in 1 Samuel 17. He was defeated by David, a young Israelite shepherd, who became a legendary hero in Jewish and Christian traditions. The name Goliath symbolizes courage, strength, and faith in the face of adversity.

data.cultural_impact: Goliath, as depicted in the Bible, is a symbol of human pride and strength that is ultimately conquered by a smaller and seemingly weaker force. This story has been retold and interpreted in various ways throughout history, influencing art, literature, and film. It teaches us about the importance of resilience in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Goliath represents the forces of evil in our lives, the challenges that seem too great for us to overcome on our own. Through the story of David and Goliath, we are reminded of the power of faith and trust in God. By relying on God's strength rather than our own, we can face even the greatest challenges and emerge victorious.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Goliath represents the seemingly insurmountable challenge or giant obstacle that stands before us, challenging our faith and courage. Through David's victory over Goliath, we are reminded that with God on our side, even the greatest adversities can be overcome.

historical_references.context: Goliath was a Philistine giant who challenged the Israelites to send a champion to fight him in a duel.
